newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks rise 1.76 pct to record close.
newsitem.headline: French stocks rise 1.76 pct to record close.

text.p: French stocks set a new closing record on Friday after a rally fuelled by the dollar's strength.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 52.41 points, or 1.76 percent, at 3,025.94.
Its last closing record, set on Wednesday, was 3,003.53 points.
The CAC also hit an all time intraday high of 3,030.62 on Friday.
"We're being pulled up by the dollar and by the government's pragmatism on the euro that has reassured the markets," a broker said.
The CAC-40 July futures contract rose 49 points to 3,028.

* PSA Peugeot Citroen shares rose 7.25 percent to 695 francs, their highest level this year, after brokerage Cheuvreux de Virieu raised its rating on the stock to buy from sell, underscoring a shift in sentiment on the French car sector due in part to favourable currency movements. Renault rose 1.62 percent. It hit a year high on Wednesday.

* LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton underperformed, climbing 1.05 percent to 1,629 francs, despite a rejection from Guinness and Grand Metropolitan to its proposal for a three-way drinks merger and a de-merger of their beer and food businesses.
LVMH said it would continue pushing its plan and trying to build support among shareholders in the British groups.
The British signalled they were still open to negotiations.
* Schneider rose 5.71 percent to 359 francs after better than expected first-half sales, which rose 8.8 percent on a like for like basis and 6.5 percent in France.
